findings.description: rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but seven objects (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, value). Only the first six are copied, so the propagated command is `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` with no value. HSETEX arity is -6 so processCommand accepts it, then hsetexParseArgs rejects FIELDS because i >= argc-3 and replies with a wrong-arity error. Replicas therefore do not apply the increment (CRITICAL log, optional panic via propagation-error-behavior) and AOF reload of the same command fails, so master and replica/AOF diverge and the new float is lost.
findings.failureMode: Replica apply and AOF load of rewritten HINCRBYFLOAT fail with wrong-arity; increment is not applied off-master.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT rewrite drops the new field value

findings.description: hashTypeSet for HINCRBYFLOAT dropped HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL, which hincrby still uses. On a hash with field expiration (listpack_ex or HT), hashTypeSet without that flag calls listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL) or hfieldPersist, so a successful HINCRBYFLOAT on the master deletes the field's TTL even though the command is supposed to preserve it. That is a mainline regression independent of the replication rewrite.
findings.failureMode: HINCRBYFLOAT on a field with a TTL clears that TTL on the executing primary.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT no longer keeps field TTL on the primary

findings.description:
extractSlotFromKeysResult now loops `j` from 0 through `keys_result->numkeys` inclusive (`j <= numkeys`) and indexes both `keys[j]` and `slot_buffer[j]`. Those arrays are length `numkeys` (valid indexes 0..numkeys-1); the previous code used `j < numkeys`.

Failure: for a one-key command such as `GET foo`, the extra iteration reads `keys[1]` (zeroed `pos==0`) and hashes argv[0] ("GET") as a second key, so the function returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT. preprocessCommand then sets CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT and cluster clients get a CROSSSLOT error on ordinary same-slot commands. For `numkeys >= MAX_KEYS_BUFFER` (6), `keys[numkeys]` and `slot_buffer[numkeys]` are out-of-bounds (stack or heap), which is a reachable crash/memory corruption on MGET/MSET/DEL with 6+ keys.

Fix the loop bound to `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Same-slot commands are rejected as CROSSSLOT; commands with 6+ keys crash via out-of-bounds access.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop over-reads keys and overflows slot_buffer

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult allocates `slot_buffer` with `malloc` and frees it with `free`. AGENTS.md mandate 2 requires zmalloc/zfree in src/ (outside zmalloc.c) so allocations are accounted and OOM is handled. The buffer is also never read, but the store `slot_buffer[j] = this_slot` will NULL-dereference if malloc fails. Use zmalloc/zfree, or remove the unused buffer.
findings.failureMode: slot_buffer is allocated with libc malloc/free, so Redis used_memory does not track it; a NULL malloc return is then written through and crashes.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free used instead of zmalloc/zfree

findings.description: On iOS 17+, tearDown returns early when the test name contains testSelectBottomPlacement or the device is an iPad. That return sits before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(), so those steps never run. On iPad this hits every OnboardingTests case, including testFirstRunTourDarkMode which leaves Dark theme applied. The leftover process and theme then leak into later tests. The intended skip was only switchThemeToDarkOrLight; terminate and super.tearDown must still run.
findings.failureMode: OnboardingTests tearDown on iPad or after testSelectBottomPlacement leaves the app running and skips XCTest cleanup, so later tests inherit leftover UI and theme state.
findings.title: tearDown return skips app terminate and super cleanup

findings.description: Renaming testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders drops the XCTest test prefix, so the method is never collected or run. Nothing calls it, and FullFunctionalTestPlan still includes ShareLongPressTests. TestRail case 2864380 therefore no longer executes. Restore the test prefix.
findings.failureMode: XCTest does not discover or run the bookmarks Reminders share case, so that coverage silently disappears from the suite.
findings.title: Reminders bookmark share test is no longer discovered

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>, and prepare_tools uses `?` while returning crate::Result<PathBuf>. crate::Error implements From<io::Error> and From<anyhow::Error> only; `?` performs a single From conversion, so FileWriteError does not convert. This is a Linux compile failure for tauri-bundler. Keep returning std::io::Error or add a real From into crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: `cargo build` of tauri-bundler on Linux fails with E0277: FileWriteError is not convertible to crate::Error via `?`.
findings.title: FileWriteError cannot convert into crate::Error

findings.description: prepare_tools writes linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh only when the cached file already exists (`if gtk.exists()`). AppImage bundling always passes `--plugin gtk`, so a first-time or clean-cache run never materializes the inlined plugin and linuxdeploy fails looking up the gtk plugin. The gstreamer branch correctly uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`. Restore the negated existence check (or always overwrite from include_bytes).
findings.failureMode: First AppImage bundle with an empty tools cache never writes linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh, so `linuxdeploy --plugin gtk` fails and bundling aborts.
findings.title: GTK plugin is skipped on first AppImage bundle

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write. set_permissions errors with NotFound when the path does not exist. AppRun, linuxdeploy, the gstreamer plugin, and the appimage plugin are all written only on the `if !path.exists()` path, so the first download/install of each tool fails instead of creating an executable file. Write the bytes first, then chmod, as the base did.
findings.failureMode: First-time AppImage bundling cannot create AppRun/linuxdeploy/plugin files because chmod on a missing path returns NotFound.
findings.title: set_permissions before write fails for new tool files

findings.description: `POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite` is decorated with `@Roles("TEAM_MEMBER")`. RolesGuard treats that as the minimum role, and TEAM_ROLES are ordered OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER, so any accepted team member satisfies the guard. The org analog uses `@Roles("TEAM_ADMIN")`, TRPC `createInvite` requires OWNER/ADMIN, and the new e2e cases expect 403 for members. Any team member can therefore mint invite tokens and add users.
findings.failureMode: Authorization bypass: non-admin team members can create team invite links
findings.title: Invite endpoint authorizes TEAM_MEMBER instead of TEAM_ADMIN

findings.description: TeamService.createInvite now returns `newToken.identifier` (`invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`) as `token` instead of the generated hex secret. The identifier is a predictable per-team string, identical on every create, and is not what `inviteMemberByToken` looks up (`VerificationToken.token`). Invite links are still built from the hex, so `data.token` is not present in `inviteLink` and cannot be redeemed. This is the mainline create path for the new v2 endpoint, the org invite endpoint, and TRPC createInvite when no existing token is supplied.
findings.failureMode: API and TRPC invite creation return a non-secret identifier that cannot be used to join the team
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of secret token

findings.description: `buildInviteLink` now returns the `/teams?token=` URL when `isOrgContext` is true and the `/signup?token=` getting-started URL when it is false. Previously the condition was `if (!isOrgContext)`, so regular teams received `/teams` and organization/org-team invites received `/signup`. After this change, regular-team invites send users to signup/onboarding and org invites send users to `/teams`, so invitees land on the wrong flow.
findings.failureMode: Generated invite URLs use the opposite route for team vs organization context
findings.title: Invite link org/team routing condition is inverted

findings.description: `write_and_make_executable` now returns `Result<(), FileWriteError>`, and `prepare_tools` still returns `crate::Result<PathBuf>` and uses `?` on those calls. `crate::Error` has `From` impls for `io::Error` and `anyhow::Error`, but not for the new private `FileWriteError`; `?` performs only a single `From` conversion. The Linux-only AppImage module therefore fails to type-check. Previously the helper returned `std::io::Result`, which converted via `#[from] io::Error`. Fix: return `std::io::Result<()>` (or add a real `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error`).
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux because write_and_make_executable's FileWriteError cannot be converted to crate::Error at the ? sites in prepare_tools.
findings.title: FileWriteError cannot convert through prepare_tools ?

findings.description: The GTK plugin install condition was inverted from `if !gtk.exists()` to `if gtk.exists()`. On a clean tools cache the file is absent, so the inlined `linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh` is never written. `bundle_project` always passes `--plugin gtk` to linuxdeploy, so first-time (and any cache-miss) AppImage builds fail looking up the plugin. The gstreamer path still correctly uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`, which shows the GTK polarity change is accidental. Fix: restore `if !gtk.exists()`, or always overwrite the cached script with the inlined bytes.
findings.failureMode: First-time AppImage bundling skips writing linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh, so linuxdeploy --plugin gtk cannot find the plugin and the bundle fails.
findings.title: GTK plugin is never installed on first AppImage bundle

findings.description: `write_and_make_executable` now calls `fs::set_permissions` before `fs::write`. Callers invoke it only when the target does not exist (AppRun, linuxdeploy, gstreamer plugin, AppImage plugin). `set_permissions` requires an existing path, so the first AppImage bundle fails with a permissions error and never writes the tool. Previously the function wrote first, then chmod'd. Fix: write the bytes first, then set mode 0o770.
findings.failureMode: First-time writes of AppRun, linuxdeploy, and plugin scripts fail with ENOENT because chmod is attempted on a path that does not exist yet.
findings.title: set_permissions runs before the file is created

findings.description: `FileWriteError` is a new custom error enum that manually implements `Display` and `std::error::Error` instead of `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]` with `#[error(...)]`. Repository mandate 8 requires all custom error enums to use thiserror. This is independent of the missing `From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error` compile break: even if a From impl were added, the type would still violate the mandate. Fix: derive thiserror (or drop the type and return `io::Result`).
findings.failureMode: The new custom error enum violates the repository thiserror mandate and is not wired into crate::Error.
findings.title: FileWriteError implements Error by hand instead of thiserror

findings.description: The new `fs::set_permissions(...).map_err(FileWriteError::Permissions)?;` line is 101 characters. Repository rustfmt.toml sets max_width=100, and mandate 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass. Fix: wrap the line so rustfmt is satisfied.
findings.failureMode: cargo fmt --all -- --check fails on appimage/mod.rs because the new set_permissions line is 101 columns.
findings.title: New Rust line exceeds rustfmt max_width

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn models availability.days as string[], but Prisma Availability.days is Int[] and getScheduleListItemData requires days: number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper maps API schedules through that helper, so the new return type disagrees with the list-schedules mainline path and with the original inferred handler type.
findings.failureMode: useAtomGetAllSchedules data is not assignable to getScheduleListItemData (days: number[]), causing a type-check failure and wrong consumer typing of weekday indexes.
findings.title: Availability days typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: The relocated Slot type declares userIds as string[], but the deleted source type and every producer (slots util, calendars SlotInfo, getSlots) use number[]. Integrators of onTimeslotsLoaded and other Slot consumers will treat host IDs as strings and can pass the wrong shape back to APIs that expect numbers.
findings.failureMode: Consumers of Slot (onTimeslotsLoaded and tests) type userIds as strings while the slots API and former trpc Slot type provide number[]; type-correct string handling then disagrees with runtime numbers.
findings.title: Slot.userIds typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: GetAvailableSlotsResponse.SlotInfo sets fromUser.id to string, but IFromUser in getUserAvailability uses id: number and that is what _getAvailableSlots returns. useAvailableSlots now exposes this local type, so callers of the available-slots hook type the out-of-office from-user id incorrectly.
findings.failureMode: useAvailableSlots types fromUser.id as string while the availability service emits numeric IDs, so consumers write string logic against number values.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id typed as string instead of number

findings.description: setupToolbarConstraints previously set toolbar.leadingAnchor equal to leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor (the container leading edge) and toolbar.trailingAnchor equal to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor. This change replaces only the leading partner with rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor, so both edges of the live toolbar attach to the off-screen right skeleton. Combined with the skeleton width (container width minus UX.skeletonBarWidthOffset) the leading edge sits to the right of the trailing edge. This is not a rename: left and right skeleton bars are distinct views, and the feature is reached whenever toolbarHelper.isSwipingTabsEnabled is true.
findings.failureMode: When swiping tabs is enabled, Auto Layout pins the address toolbar leading edge to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailing and its trailing edge to rightSkeletonAddressBar.leading, producing a negative-width toolbar and unsatisfiable constraints. The URL bar does not fill the container and the swipe-tab skeleton layout is broken.
findings.title: Swipe-tabs toolbar leading edge pinned to the right skeleton bar

findings.description: The pageActionStack rename was applied incorrectly in updateToolbarLayout. The stacks array previously ended with pageActionStack.arrangedSubviews; it now concatenates browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews a second time instead of trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews. updateActionStack sets alpha to 0 for any button not already in its stack, then relies on this list to restore alpha to 1. Trailing page-action buttons (reload, stop loading, reader mode, summarizer) are therefore never faded in on either the animated or non-animated path, so they remain invisible after first insertion or after an action swap.
findings.failureMode: After trailing page actions are created or swapped (reload, stop, reader mode, summarizer), those buttons are left at alpha 0 because updateToolbarLayout no longer includes trailingPageActionStack. Users browsing a page do not see the reload/stop/reader-mode controls in the address bar.
findings.title: Trailing page-action buttons stay invisible after layout updates

findings.description: updateActionSpacing previously set hasPageActions from pageActionStack (the trailing stack adjacent to locationDividerView). After the rename it reads leadingPageActionStack instead of trailingPageActionStack. The divider sits between locationView and trailingPageActionStack, so its width should follow trailing actions. Concrete case: trailing reload/stop present and leading empty (AddressBarStateTests loading-state path, SampleBrowser default UX) now forces divider width 0; the reverse occupancy shows a 4pt divider with no trailing buttons.
findings.failureMode: With AddressToolbarUXConfiguration.default() (divider width 4), the divider between the URL field and trailing page actions appears when leading actions exist and disappears when only trailing actions exist. Reload/reader-mode-only states lose the divider; share-only states show a stray gap.
findings.title: Address-bar divider width keyed off leading instead of trailing actions

findings.description: This change sets compilerOptions.strict to false in the app tsconfig that `validate:types` (`tsc -b --noEmit`) and `build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) use. Repository mandate 11 requires strict mode enabled; the previous value was true. With strict off, nullish, implicit-any, and related type errors in src/ are no longer rejected, so invalid frontend code can pass CI typechecking.
findings.failureMode: The ui-v2 typecheck pipeline no longer runs in strict mode, so previously-rejected type errors compile and can ship.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled for ui-v2

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields always binds Status to `trigger.expect`. Flow-run-state and DeploymentStatusTriggerFields write Proactive selections to `trigger.after` and Reactive selections to `trigger.expect`. Backend Proactive triggers fire on the absence of `expect` events; with empty `after` they start immediately. Selecting Work pool status, Stays in, Ready therefore submits `{posture:\"Proactive\", expect:[\"prefect.work-pool.ready\"]}` and fires if no ready event occurs in the window, including when the pool is already not-ready, instead of watching after a ready event.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-pool status automation fires on absence of the selected status from t=0, not after the resource enters that status.
findings.title: Work-pool status always writes trigger.expect

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields always binds Status to `trigger.expect`, unlike DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields which store Proactive values on `trigger.after`. Selecting Work queue status \u2192 Stays in \u2192 Ready submits `{posture:\"Proactive\", expect:[\"prefect.work-queue.ready\"]}` with empty `after`, so the backend starts immediately and fires if no ready event occurs \u2014 including when the queue never entered Ready. Patching only the work-pool component would leave this path broken.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-queue status automation fires on absence of the selected status from t=0, not after the resource enters that status.
findings.title: Work-queue status always writes trigger.expect

findings.description: The textarea splits on newlines and always calls `field.onChange` with a non-empty array because `\"\".split(\"\\n\")` is `[\"\"]` (`lines.length > 0` is therefore dead). Leaving Expected Events blank, or clearing it, submits `expect: [\"\"]`. Backend `EventTrigger.expects()` treats a non-empty expect set as required exact matches; `\"\"` matches no real event, so the automation never fires. An omitted/empty expect set would match any event. Trailing blank lines also inject empty strings into otherwise valid lists.
findings.failureMode: Clearing Expected Events stores [\"\"] so the trigger matches no events instead of matching any event.
findings.title: Empty custom events become a never-matching [""]

findings.description: `statusFieldName` switches between `trigger.expect` (Reactive) and `trigger.after` (Proactive), but the previously written array is never copied or cleared. A user who selects Not Ready then switches to Stays in still has `expect: [\"prefect.deployment.not-ready\"]` while the Select reads empty `after`; submitting yields a Proactive trigger with empty `after` (starts immediately) and leftover `expect`. Re-selecting a status writes `after` without clearing `expect`, producing both fields populated. Either payload differs from the visible Status value.
findings.failureMode: Switching Enters/Stays in leaves the chosen status on the old field and shows an empty Status control, so the submitted after/expect pair is wrong.
findings.title: Deployment status is not moved when posture changes

findings.description: The previous keyword pattern ran `keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape')` and doubled `\\u` so a search for CJK/emoji would match `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=True)` storage (`\\uXXXX` in workflow_runs.inputs/outputs). Production writers still use default `json.dumps` (ensure_ascii=True) in sqlalchemy_workflow_execution_repository.py and workflow_execution_tasks.py. The new `escape_like_pattern(keyword_trimmed)` keeps the raw characters, so `ilike('%你好%')` does not match stored `\\u4f60\\u597d` and the log search returns empty. Restore unicode_escape (or dump JSON with ensure_ascii=False) so the LIKE pattern matches the stored form, then apply LIKE escaping.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow logs with non-ASCII keywords returns no matching runs even when those characters are in inputs/outputs.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search no longer matches unicode JSON

findings.description: The LIKE fallback now escapes %, _, and \\ via escape_like_pattern (backslash as the escape character) but compiles `WHERE text LIKE ? ESCAPE '|'`. Because the ESCAPE character is `|`, backslash-escaped `\%`/`\_` remain wildcards, so a query such as `50%` still matches `500`/`50X`, and a query containing `|` can swallow the next character. Fix: either use `ESCAPE '\\'` to match the helper, or keep `ESCAPE '|'` and escape `|`, `%`, and `_` with `|` instead of calling escape_like_pattern.
findings.failureMode: Full-text LIKE fallback searches treat % and _ as wildcards and mis-handle |, returning wrong documents.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE escape character does not match helper escaping

findings.description: The public pool now uses vmImage macOS-15 (internal pool image at line 322). Both macOS jobs still run `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` (lines 166 and 392). Hosted macOS-15 images install Xcode 16.4 at /Applications/Xcode_16.4.app and do not ship Xcode_15.2.0.app, so the step exits non-zero and the job never builds. The updated display names at lines 167 and 393 already say Xcode 16.4.0; the path was not updated.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs fail at xcode-select because Xcode_15.2.0.app is not installed on macOS-15
findings.title: macOS-15 image has no Xcode 15.2.0

findings.description: The BUILD002 error used to fire on every servicing build that dropped a baseline package reference. This hunk adds `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'`, so the check runs only on the first servicing patch and is skipped for 10.0.2 and later. Nearby first-patch special cases use `!= '1'` (for example TargetingPackVersion in GenerateFiles). If the intent was to exempt patch 1 while the 10.0 baseline is still 9.0.0, the comparison is inverted and 10.0.1 still errors; if the intent was to keep the servicing invariant, the conjunct should not be added. Either way, later servicing updates can remove package references with no BUILD002 failure.
findings.failureMode: After 10.0.1, servicing builds can drop package references without BUILD002; if == '1' was meant to be != '1', this 10.0.1 build still hits BUILD002 against the 9.0.0 baseline
findings.title: BUILD002 patch gate is inverted

findings.description: The file previously used a file-scoped namespace (`namespace ...;`) and this diff wraps the types in a traditional block-scoped namespace. Repository rule 2 requires file-scoped namespace declarations in every C# file.
findings.failureMode: Changed C# file uses a block-scoped namespace, violating the file-scoped namespace mandate
findings.title: Test file switched to a block-scoped namespace

findings.description: The migrated Slot type sets userIds to string[], but the deleted trpc Slot and all slot-generation code (packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts, packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/util.ts) use number[]. BookerPlatformWrapperAtomProps.onTimeslotsLoaded is typed with this Slot, so platform callers that filter or compare userIds as strings get no matches against the numeric IDs the API actually returns. Restore userIds?: number[].
findings.failureMode: Consumers of Slot (onTimeslotsLoaded and @calcom/atoms/booker/types) treat host user IDs as strings, but slot generation still emits number[]. String comparisons and typed callbacks then miss matching hosts.
findings.title: Slot.userIds typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: The local GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn sets availability.days to string[], but Prisma Availability.days is Int[] and the previous Awaited handler return inferred number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper maps this data through getScheduleListItemData, whose Schedule type requires days: number[], and availabilityAsString does day - 1 arithmetic. Change days to number[].
findings.failureMode: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn types weekday indexes as strings, so schedule list data is not assignable to getScheduleListItemData/availabilityAsString which require number[] and do numeric day arithmetic.
findings.title: Availability days typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: GetAvailableSlotsResponse.SlotInfo types fromUser.id as string, but IFromUser.id (and toUser.id in the same type) is number. useAvailableSlots now returns this local type, and EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes that data into useAvailableTimeSlots which expects IGetAvailableSlots with numeric fromUser.id. Restore fromUser.id to number so the copied contract matches the slots API.
findings.failureMode: useAvailableSlots types fromUser.id as string while the API returns a number, so typed consumers compare against the wrong primitive and miss OOO/redirect host identity.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id typed as string instead of number

findings.description: The guard was changed from `json || json5` to `json && json5`. A path extension cannot be both, so the block never runs, `config_schema_validator` is never used, and invalid JSON/JSON5 configs no longer log schema errors or `exit(1)` before deserialize.
findings.failureMode: Every tauri.conf.json/json5 load skips schema validation that previously rejected invalid configs.
findings.title: Schema validation condition is impossible

findings.description: The lookup was changed from `config.get("identifier")` to `config.get("bundle")`. In tauri.conf.json the app id is the top-level string `identifier`; `bundle` is an object, so `.and_then(|id| id.as_str())` always yields None. `write_options`/`read_options` then fail with "app configuration is missing an identifier" on every `tauri android|ios dev|build` run.
findings.failureMode: Mobile CLI option IPC setup always errors because original_identifier is None even when identifier is present.
findings.title: original_identifier reads bundle instead of identifier

findings.description: The OnceLock initializer is a 156-column statement. rustfmt.toml sets max_width=100, so `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this new line. The previous schema parse was already wrapped.
findings.failureMode: cargo fmt --check fails on crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/config.rs.
findings.title: New validator line exceeds rustfmt max_width

findings.description: The require was changed from `../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink` to `../../lib/magic-link/magic-link`, but the file is still `lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js` (not renamed in this PR). Node cannot resolve the kebab-case path, so requiring members-api fails immediately with MODULE_NOT_FOUND.
findings.failureMode: Loading MembersAPI throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND because magic-link.js does not exist; member signup/signin and related APIs cannot start.
findings.title: MagicLink require path does not exist

findings.description: init() now requires `../email-service/email-event-storage`, but the file is still `email-service/EmailEventStorage.js` (not renamed in this PR). The kebab-case path does not resolve, so wrapper initialization crashes.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND, so email analytics never starts and open/delivery tracking jobs cannot run.
findings.title: EmailEventStorage require path does not exist

findings.description: init() now requires `../email-service/email-event-processor`, but the file is still `email-service/EmailEventProcessor.js` (not renamed in this PR). The kebab-case path does not resolve.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND even if the storage path were fixed, so email analytics never starts.
findings.title: EmailEventProcessor require path does not exist

findings.description: The rename hunk removed trailing semicolons from the first ten require statements (lines 1-9). Mandate 19 requires explicit semicolons on all JS statements. Restore `;` on each require. Affected lines: 1-9.
findings.failureMode: These statements now rely on ASI, violating the repository mandate that JavaScript statements end with explicit semicolons.
findings.title: Require statements dropped required semicolons

findings.description:
rewriteClientCommandVector is called with argc 6 but seven objects (HSETEX, key, KEEPTTL, FIELDS, 1, field, value). Only the first six are copied, so the propagated command is `HSETEX <key> KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 <field>` with no value.

HSETEX arity -6 accepts that vector, then hsetexParseArgs rejects it (`FIELDS` at index 3 with argc 6 trips `i >= argc-3`) via addReplyErrorArity. Replicas (CLIENT_MASTER) and AOF fake clients discard replies, so the increment is silently not applied. After failover or AOF replay the field keeps the pre-increment value (or is missing if it was created by HINCRBYFLOAT). Fix: pass argc 7 so `newobj` is included.
findings.failureMode: Replica and AOF receive a valueless HSETEX and silently skip the HINCRBYFLOAT update, causing master/replica and AOF divergence.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT replication rewrite drops the new field value

findings.description:
hashTypeSet for HINCRBYFLOAT dropped HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL and now passes only HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE. rewriteClientCommandVector only rewrites the command for AOF/replication after the master already mutated the hash; it does not re-run HSETEX KEEPTTL locally.

On listpack_ex, missing KEEP_TTL calls listpackExUpdateExpiry(..., HASH_LP_NO_TTL); on HT it calls hfieldPersist(). So `HSETEX k EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1` then `HINCRBYFLOAT k f 1.1` leaves the new value on the master with no expiration (HTTL/HPTTL -1), breaking the existing contract covered by `HINCRBYFLOAT - preserve expiration time of the field`. Restore HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE | HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL.
findings.failureMode: A hash field with a TTL loses that TTL on the master as soon as HINCRBYFLOAT updates it.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT on the master no longer keeps field TTL

findings.description: The diff removes static from addHashFieldToReply. Every remaining call and the definition still live only in src/t_hash.c, and server.h has no prototype. Mandate 7 requires file-local helpers to stay static; this exports a t_hash.c-only symbol (returning file-local GetFieldRes) for no new caller. Restore static.
findings.failureMode: A file-local helper is exported, violating the static-helper mandate and polluting the global symbol table.
findings.title: addHashFieldToReply lost static without gaining external callers

findings.description: This diff sets compilerOptions.strict to false in tsconfig.app.json, which is the config used by `tsc -b` (`validate:types` and `npm run build`). AGENTS.md requires strict mode enabled with no-emit type checking. The change weakens the type-checking pipeline so previously illegal code in src/ compiles and ships. Restore `"strict": true`.
findings.failureMode: validate:types and production builds no longer fail on strict type errors across ui-v2
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled for ui-v2

findings.description: WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields always binds Status to `trigger.expect`. DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields write Proactive selections to `trigger.after` (empty expect), which is how “Stays in” is encoded. A user who picks Work pool status, Posture “Stays in”, and Status “Not Ready” therefore submits expect=["prefect.work-pool.not-ready"] with empty after. A Proactive trigger with empty after starts immediately and fires when those expected events are absent—the inverse of “stays not-ready”. Bind Status to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive and `trigger.expect` when Reactive, matching deployment-status.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-pool automations fire on absence of the selected status instead of the pool staying in that status
findings.title: Proactive work-pool status writes expect instead of after

findings.description: WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields always binds Status to `trigger.expect`. DeploymentStatusTriggerFields and FlowRunStateTriggerFields write Proactive selections to `trigger.after`. A user who picks Work queue status, Posture “Stays in”, and Status “Not Ready” therefore submits expect=["prefect.work-queue.not-ready"] with empty after. A Proactive trigger with empty after starts immediately and fires when those expected events are absent—the inverse of “stays not-ready”. Bind Status to `trigger.after` when posture is Proactive and `trigger.expect` when Reactive.
findings.failureMode: Proactive work-queue automations fire on absence of the selected status instead of the queue staying in that status
findings.title: Proactive work-queue status writes expect instead of after

findings.description: statusFieldName flips between trigger.after and trigger.expect, but the previous array is never copied or cleared. Default posture is Reactive, so selecting Ready writes expect=["prefect.deployment.ready"]. Switching to Stays in rebinds the Select to trigger.after (UI goes empty) while expect stays set; picking Ready again writes after without clearing expect. The submitted Proactive trigger then has after and expect both equal to that status. The engine treats that as a special same-event case (bucket starts at -1) instead of “stayed in” that status (after set, expect empty). Clear the unused field (or move the value) when posture changes.
findings.failureMode: Switching Enters/Stays in after picking a status submits both after and expect, so Proactive deployment automations fire on the wrong condition
findings.title: Posture switch leaves status in the unused after/expect field

findings.description: onChange splits the textarea on newlines and writes the result whenever length > 0. `"".split("\n")` is `[""]` and a trailing Enter yields `["event", ""]`, so clearing Expected Events or pressing Enter on an empty box stores empty strings in `trigger.expect`. The backend treats a non-empty expect set as real criteria (`expects("")` matches no real event). A user who types then deletes the field, or only presses Enter, therefore gets a Reactive automation that never fires (or a Proactive one that fires every window) instead of empty-expect “match any event”. The UI still shows a blank textarea because `[""].join("\n")` is `""`. Filter blank lines and store undefined/[] when none remain.
findings.failureMode: Empty or trailing-newline textarea values become expect=[""], so Reactive custom triggers never match and Proactive ones fire on every window
findings.title: Custom expected-events textarea stores empty strings

findings.description: After Action.SelectLightTheme, the test reads AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.darkThemeView and asserts its value is "1". SelectLightTheme taps LightThemeView, and GenericImageOption exposes accessibilityValue "1" only on the selected option, so DarkThemeView remains "0" and XCTAssertEqual fails on the happy path. The local comment, variable name lightIsSelected, the matching dark/automatic assertions, and the pre-change lightThemeView read all require LightThemeView here.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails after a successful light-theme selection because it reads DarkThemeView instead of LightThemeView
findings.title: Light-theme assertion checks dark theme control

findings.description: After Action.SelectLightTheme, testCheckSystemThemeChanges reads AccessibilityIdentifiers.Settings.Appearance.darkThemeView and asserts its value is "1". ThemeOptionView maps light to lightThemeView and dark to darkThemeView, and GenericImageOption exposes accessibilityValue "1" only when that option is selected. Selecting Light therefore leaves darkThemeView at "0", so the assertion fails on the Full Functional path that still runs this test. The identifier should be lightThemeView, matching the pre-change assertion and the SelectDarkTheme check that follows.
findings.failureMode: testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails immediately after selecting Light because the dark theme control is not selected
findings.title: Light theme assertion queries the dark theme control

findings.description: The hunk deleted `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` from before the Done tap and reinserted it after, so testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection now calls app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap() while still on TopSitesSettingsViewController. That child screen never sets a Done item; only HomePageSettingViewController and AppSettingsTableViewController do. The previous order matched the working pattern in validateNumberOfTopSitesDisplayed (goto NewTabScreen, then Done), which pops back to a screen that actually has Done. waitAndTap will time out looking for Done on Shortcuts, failing the Full Functional run of this test.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection times out waiting for a Done button that is not on the Shortcuts screen
findings.title: Done is tapped on Shortcuts, which has no Done button

findings.description: The new iPad/testSelectBottomPlacement guard uses `return`, so it skips the rest of tearDown rather than only skipping switchThemeToDarkOrLight. On iOS 17+, that path is taken for every OnboardingTests case on iPad and for testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone, so app.terminate() and super.tearDown() never run. Subsequent tests can inherit a live app, leftover theme/toolbar state, and an incomplete XCTest teardown. The skip should fall through to terminate/super.tearDown() instead of returning.
findings.failureMode: On iOS 17+, every OnboardingTests run on iPad, and testSelectBottomPlacement on iPhone, return from tearDown before app.terminate() and super.tearDown(). The app and XCTest lifecycle are left unclean for later tests.
findings.title: tearDown returns early and skips app cleanup

findings.description: Renaming testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders to verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders drops the XCTest `test` prefix, so the method is no longer a test. Nothing else calls it, and FullFunctionalTestPlan still runs ShareLongPressTests, so the bookmark long-press \u2192 Reminders coverage (TestRail 2864380) disappears from CI. Restore the `test` prefix.
findings.failureMode: XCTest does not discover verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders, so TestRail 2864380 / bookmark share-to-Reminders is never run in FullFunctional or any other plan.
findings.title: Bookmarks Reminders test is no longer executed

findings.description: CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer.render_template only rejects non-string values when the value is not None, then returns rendered unconditionally. result.get("result") is None when the key is missing or the value is None, so the function returns None while being annotated to return str. TemplateTransformNode._run immediately does len(rendered); that TypeError is not converted to a failed NodeRunResult. basedpyright reports: Type "str | None" is not assignable to return type "str". Fix: treat None like any non-string (raise TemplateRenderError) so the method always returns str.
findings.failureMode: If execute_workflow_code_template omits "result" or sets it to None, render_template returns None. TemplateTransformNode._run then calls len(rendered) and raises TypeError instead of a TemplateRenderError failure. basedpyright also fails reportReturnType because str | None is returned as str.
findings.title: Renderer can return None, crashing length check

findings.description: CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer.render_template is annotated to return str, but after `rendered = result.get("result")` it only rejects non-None non-strings. If the executor returns `{}` or `{"result": None}` (reachable via an injected code_executor, and inferred by basedpyright as `str | None`), the method returns None. TemplateTransformNode._run then executes `len(rendered)`, which raises TypeError instead of a TemplateRenderError-backed FAILED NodeRunResult. `uv run --directory api --dev basedpyright` also fails with reportReturnType on `return rendered`, so `make type-check` does not pass. Fix: treat any non-str (including None) as TemplateRenderError, e.g. `if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)`.
findings.failureMode: Missing or None template result is returned as None; _run then TypeErrors on len(None), and basedpyright reportReturnType fails type-check.
findings.title: Renderer returns None, crashing length check

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction instead of .readerMode. ToolbarMiddleware, accessibilityPerformMagicTap, and summarizer long-press all dispatch GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode expecting a reader-mode toggle. BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions maps .readerModeLongPressAction to toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which creates a reading-list record. Restore displayView: .readerMode so the tap path still calls toggleReaderMode().
findings.failureMode: Tapping the reader-mode button, VoiceOver magic tap, or long-pressing the summarizer button dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, which now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction. BrowserViewController then calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() and adds the page to the reading list instead of toggleReaderMode(), so reader mode never opens or closes.
findings.title: Reader mode tap now adds to reading list

findings.description: cancelEditMode changed the guard from (isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL) to (isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL). Reader-mode URLs are http localhost pages, so they now pass through instead of being niled. handleCancelEditAction uses toolbarAction.url ?? state.url, so the internal reader-mode URL overwrites the displayed article URL. Restore the exclusion of isReaderModeURL.
findings.failureMode: While a page is in reader mode, tapping tabs, menu, or cancel-edit dispatches ToolbarActionType.cancelEdit with the raw tab URL (http://localhost/reader-mode/page). AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction writes that URL into the address bar, replacing the decoded article URL that displayURL previously showed.
findings.title: Cancel edit keeps internal reader-mode URL

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry inverted the switch: case .available is now false and default is true, while the comment still says the button will be enabled after the action. ToolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped maps isEnabled into ReaderModeButtonTappedExtra.isPrivate, so every reader-mode tap now records the wrong is_private extra (nil/.active report is_private=true; .available reports is_private=false). testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes asserts savedExtras.isPrivate == false against default state and will fail. Restore case .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: A reader-mode toolbar tap records toolbar.reader_mode_button_tapped with is_private inverted relative to the previous mapping, and ToolbarMiddlewareTests.testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes fails because default state now yields savedExtras.isPrivate == true.
findings.title: Reader mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description:
The new loop in extractSlotFromKeysResult iterates `j <= keys_result->numkeys` instead of `j < keys_result->numkeys`. The extra iteration reads `keys_result->keys[numkeys]`, which is past the prepared key list, and also writes one past `slot_buffer`.

For 1–5 keys (stored in keysbuf after GETKEYS_RESULT_INIT), that extra slot is leftover zeros so `pos` is 0: argv[0] (the command name) is hashed as a key. A single-key command such as SET/GET then compares the real key’s slot with the command-name slot and, when they differ, returns CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT. preprocessCommand marks CLIENT_READ_CROSS_SLOT, and asmFeedMigrationClient cancels slot migration. Ordinary same-slot commands are rejected as CROSSSLOT.

For 6 keys the extra index is past keysbuf[MAX_KEYS_BUFFER]; for more than 6 it is past the heap allocation sized exactly to numkeys. Both are reachable crashes on commands such as DEL/MSET/MGET with many keys.

Fix the bound to `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Off-by-one reads past the key array, producing false CROSSSLOT errors on ordinary commands and crashing when there are 6+ keys.
findings.title: Off-by-one overruns keys when extracting slots

findings.description:
extractSlotFromKeysResult now allocates with libc malloc (line 1110) and releases with libc free (lines 1120 and 1124). cluster.c includes server.h, which marks malloc/free deprecated, and src/Makefile always passes -Werror=deprecated-declarations, so compiling cluster.c fails. The call also violates the zmalloc/zfree mandate, so the buffer is invisible to used_memory, and malloc’s NULL return is unchecked: on OOM the following `slot_buffer[j] = this_slot` dereferences NULL.

slot_buffer is written and never read, so the allocation is also dead. Remove it, or allocate with zmalloc and release with zfree.
findings.failureMode: Deprecated malloc/free fail the -Werror=deprecated-declarations build; allocations bypass Redis memory tracking and can NULL-deref on OOM.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free breaks the build and memory tracking

findings.description: `setupToolbarConstraints` previously pinned `toolbar.leadingAnchor` to `leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor` (which equals the container leading edge, so the live toolbar fills the bar). It now pins leading to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor`. Combined with the unchanged trailing constraint to `rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor`, that places the toolbar’s leading edge to the right of its trailing edge (right skeleton sits off-screen to the right). With swiping tabs on by default on iPhone, Auto Layout is unsatisfiable and the address toolbar does not occupy the container.
findings.failureMode: When swiping tabs is enabled, the address toolbar gets inverted/off-screen leading and trailing constraints and no longer lays out across the container.
findings.title: Swipe-tabs toolbar leading edge pinned to the right skeleton

findings.description: The `pageActionStack` rename was applied incorrectly in `updateToolbarLayout`: the fourth term of `stacks` is now `browserActionStack.arrangedSubviews` again instead of `trailingPageActionStack.arrangedSubviews`. New trailing page-action buttons (reload, reader mode, summarizer, stop) are created at `alpha = 0` and this method is what fades them to 1. Those buttons are no longer included, so on the first (and later) configure they remain fully transparent and untappable.
findings.failureMode: Address toolbar trailing actions stay at alpha 0 after configure, so reload/reader/summarizer/stop buttons never appear.
findings.title: Trailing page-action buttons stay invisible after rename

findings.description: `updateActionSpacing` used to show the location-to-actions divider when `pageActionStack` (the trailing stack next to the divider) had buttons. After the rename it checks `leadingPageActionStack` instead of `trailingPageActionStack`. With default UX (divider width 4), a toolbar that has only trailing actions (reload/stop) loses the divider, and a toolbar that has only leading actions (share/translate) gains a spurious gap before an empty trailing stack.
findings.failureMode: Address bar divider appears or disappears based on leading page actions rather than the trailing stack it actually separates.
findings.title: Page-action divider now keys off the wrong stack

findings.description: The previous pattern ran keyword[:30].encode('unicode_escape') so a search for 你好 matched json.dumps() output (ensure_ascii=True) stored in WorkflowRun.inputs/outputs. The new code only applies escape_like_pattern() to the raw keyword, so ILIKE '%你好%' does not match {\"search_term\": \"\\u4f60\\u597d\"}. ASCII tests still pass; CJK (and other non-ASCII) keyword search on MySQL, where the old backslash-escape LIKE default made unicode_escape work, now returns empty results. Restore JSON-aware matching for inputs/outputs in addition to LIKE wildcard escaping.
findings.failureMode: Searching workflow logs by a non-ASCII keyword returns no rows even when inputs/outputs contain that text, because stored JSON uses \\uXXXX sequences.
findings.title: Workflow log keyword search no longer matches JSON unicode escapes

findings.description: escape_like_pattern() prefixes \, %, and _ with backslash, but the LIKE clause declares ESCAPE '|'. A query such as "50%" becomes the bound pattern %50\%% with escape '|', so the backslash is a literal character and the trailing % is still a wildcard. Documents containing "50%" are missed, and a query containing | is parsed as an IRIS escape sequence. Use ESCAPE '\' (matching the helper) or re-escape %, _, and | with '|'.
findings.failureMode: IRIS full-text LIKE fallback treats % and _ as wildcards and requires a literal backslash, so searches for terms containing %, _, or | return wrong or empty results.
findings.title: IRIS LIKE ESCAPE character does not match helper escaping

findings.description: The new endpoint is decorated with @Roles(\"TEAM_MEMBER\"). RolesGuard treats that as a minimum role, so OWNER, ADMIN, and MEMBER all pass. Creating invites is an admin action everywhere else (org teams invite uses TEAM_ADMIN; tRPC createInvite requires OWNER/ADMIN). A regular member can therefore mint invite tokens. The accompanying e2e test expects 403 for a MEMBER, which this decorator will not produce.
findings.failureMode: Any accepted team MEMBER can POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and generate a join link; non-admin 403 is not enforced.
findings.title: Invite endpoint allows any team member

findings.description: On the new-token path, createInvite now returns `token: newToken.identifier` instead of the stored secret `token`. Identifier is the non-secret string `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`. inviteMemberByToken and acceptInvitationByToken look up VerificationToken.token, so clients that use the returned token (API v2, org invite, tRPC createInvite) cannot redeem the invite. The inviteLink is still built from the real hex token, so token and link no longer match.
findings.failureMode: Callers of TeamService.createInvite receive identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}` as data.token while inviteLink is built from the actual hex token. Sharing or looking up that token cannot join the team.
findings.title: createInvite returns identifier instead of secret token

findings.description: buildInviteLink flipped `if (!isOrgContext)` to `if (isOrgContext)`. Regular teams now get `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=...` and organization/sub-team invites now get `/teams?token=...`. Existing callers (web copy-invite-link, org API invite, this new endpoint) therefore send invitees to the wrong path: existing users of a regular team are pushed through signup, and org invitees who need signup are sent to /teams.
findings.failureMode: Regular-team invites now go to /signup and org/sub-team invites now go to /teams, so invitees land on the wrong join flow.
findings.title: Invite link org/team routing is inverted

findings.description: Public and internal macOS jobs now use macOS-15, but both still run `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer`. GitHub/Azure macOS-15 images ship Xcode 16.4 at `/Applications/Xcode_16.4.app` (and `Xcode_16.4.0.app`) and do not include Xcode 15.2, so every macOS job fails that step. Display names already say XCode 16.4.0. Fix both sites by pointing xcode-select at Xcode_16.4.0.app.
findings.failureMode: macOS CI jobs fail at the xcode-select step because /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app does not exist on macOS-15
findings.title: macOS-15 image still selects missing Xcode 15.2

findings.description: BUILD002 previously failed any servicing build that dropped a baseline package reference. This change adds `AND '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1'`. Every other patch-1 special case in-repo uses `!= '1'` (for example targeting-pack version updates). This branch just became a 10.0.1 servicing build (`IsServicingBuild` true) while Baseline.xml is still 9.0.0, so BUILD002 now runs against the 9.0 graph: Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup still baselines System.Text.Json but no longer references it, which produces a mainline BUILD002 error. After the patch is bumped to 2+, BUILD002 never runs, so later servicing updates can drop package dependencies without the documented non-suppressible check. The operator should be `!= '1'` if the intent was to skip the stale 9.0 baseline on the first servicing patch.
findings.failureMode: Servicing builds on patch 1 can fail BUILD002 against a stale 9.0 baseline, while later servicing patches no longer reject removed package references
findings.title: BUILD002 inverted so it only runs on patch 1

findings.description: The test file previously used a file-scoped namespace (`namespace ...;`). This diff wraps the file in a traditional block-scoped namespace with braces, which AGENTS.md rule 2 forbids for every C# file. Neighboring E2E tests in the same directory still use file-scoped namespaces.
findings.failureMode: Changed C# file violates the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule
findings.title: File-scoped namespace converted to block-scoped

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now assigns displayView: .readerModeLongPressAction instead of .readerMode. On the mainline tap path, ToolbarMiddleware (and accessibilityPerformMagicTap) dispatch GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode expecting a reader-mode toggle. After this change the reducer routes that action to the long-press display type, so BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() and adds the page to the reading list instead of enabling or disabling reader mode. Restore displayView: .readerMode.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the reader mode button, VoiceOver magic tap, or long-pressing the summarizer button dispatches GeneralBrowserActionType.showReaderMode, which now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction. BrowserViewController then calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction() (add to reading list) instead of toggleReaderMode() (enable/disable reader view). The page stays in its current reader-mode state and a reading-list toast/record is created instead.
findings.title: Reader mode tap now adds to reading list

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry inverted the isReaderModeEnabled mapping from `.available: true / default: false` to `.available: false / default: true` while leaving the comment that available “will be enabled after action gets executed.” Glean extra `enabled` therefore reports the opposite of whether reader mode is being opened or closed on the toolbar tap path. Restore the original mapping.
findings.failureMode: Tapping reader mode while the page is available (about to open) records Toolbar.reader_mode_button_tapped with enabled=false; tapping while already active (about to close) records enabled=true. That is the opposite of the previous post-action meaning and of the leftover comment. The existing unit test still expects enabled=false on the default nil readerModeState, which now hits default: true and fails.
findings.title: Reader mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: cancelEditMode changed from keeping the tab URL only when it is a web page and not a reader-mode URL (`isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL`) to keeping it when it is a web page or a reader-mode URL. Reader-mode URLs are http://localhost/reader-mode/page, so they now survive cancel-edit. ToolbarAction.cancelEdit then overwrites AddressBarState.url with that internal URL (handleCancelEditAction uses toolbarAction.url ?? state.url), so after opening the tab tray/menu or canceling edit in reader mode the address bar can show the localhost reader-mode URL. Restore the original exclusion of reader-mode URLs.
findings.failureMode: While a tab is in reader mode, tapping Tabs, Menu, or Cancel Edit runs cancelEditMode. The selected tab URL is http://localhost/reader-mode/page?... which isWebPage() and isReaderModeURL. The old guard dropped that URL (nil); the new OR keeps it. AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction then writes that localhost reader-mode URL into the address bar instead of leaving the decoded page URL.
findings.title: Cancel-edit keeps reader-mode internal URL

findings.description: members-api.js now requires ../../lib/magic-link/magic-link, but the only file on disk is MagicLink.js. This is not a case-only rename (hyphen vs camelCase), so Node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on every filesystem. members/api.js loads this module at startup, and boot.js awaits members.init(), so Ghost fails to boot and member auth/signup is unavailable. Other callers still correctly require MagicLink.js.
findings.failureMode: Ghost boot and members API load throw MODULE_NOT_FOUND for magic-link.js
findings.title: Members API requires magic-link file that does not exist

findings.description: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() now requires ../email-service/email-event-storage, but the module is still EmailEventStorage.js. The hyphenated path is not a case-only variant, so require throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on every filesystem. boot.js awaits emailAnalytics.init() in Promise.all, so Ghost startup fails and email analytics never starts.
findings.failureMode: Ghost boot throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND from email-event-storage require during emailAnalytics.init()
findings.title: Email analytics requires kebab-case files that were not renamed

findings.description: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() now requires ../email-service/email-event-processor, but the module is still EmailEventProcessor.js. Even if the sibling email-event-storage require is restored, this line still throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND, so email analytics initialization and Ghost boot fail.
findings.failureMode: Ghost boot throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND from email-event-processor require during emailAnalytics.init()
findings.title: Email analytics requires missing email-event-processor module

findings.description: The first ten require statements in members-api.js no longer end with semicolons (e.g. const {Router} = require('express')). Mandate 19 requires explicit semicolons on all JavaScript statements. This is a real changed-line regression versus the previous file.
findings.failureMode: Changed statements violate the repository semicolon mandate and can fail lint
findings.title: Dropped required semicolons on members-api requires

findings.description: The JSON/JSON5 schema-validation guard was changed from `||` to `&&`. A path extension cannot be both `json` and `json5`, so `config_schema_validator()` is never invoked. Loading a `tauri.conf.json` (or `.json5`) that violates the bundled schema no longer logs the schema errors or `exit(1)` on first load; the CLI either accepts the file or fails later with a less specific deserialize error. Restore `||`.
findings.failureMode: tauri.conf.json and tauri.conf.json5 are never schema-validated, so previously rejected invalid configs now proceed until serde or later, and some schema-only constraints are skipped entirely
findings.title: Schema validation never runs for JSON configs

findings.description: `original_identifier` now looks up top-level `bundle` and then treats it as a string. In v2 config JSON, `identifier` is the top-level string and `bundle` is an object, so `as_str()` is always `None`. `write_options`/`read_options` require `original_identifier()` and return `app configuration is missing an identifier`, breaking `tauri android|ios` dev/build even when the config has a valid identifier. Revert the key to `identifier`.
findings.failureMode: Mobile CLI commands fail with 'app configuration is missing an identifier' because original_identifier is always None
findings.title: original_identifier reads bundle instead of identifier

findings.description: The new OnceLock initializer packs schema parsing and expect onto a single 156-character line. rustfmt.toml sets max_width=100, so `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (mandate 3) will fail on this changed line until it is wrapped.
findings.failureMode: cargo fmt --all -- --check fails on crates/tauri-cli/src/helpers/config.rs
findings.title: New validator helper exceeds rustfmt max_width

Regular teams now get `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=...` and organization/sub-team invites now get `/teams?token=...`. Existing callers (web copy-invite-link, org API invite, this new endpoint) therefore send invitees to the wrong path: existing users of a regular team are pushed through signup, and org invitees who need signup are sent to /teams.
findings.failureMode: Regular-team invites now go to /signup and org/sub-team invites now go to /teams, so invitees land on the wrong join flow.
findings.title: Invite link org/team routing is inverted
